extracted.intended_audience: readers/contributors/reporters of errata for The Art of Computer Programming (TAOCP) Volume 4A; editors/typesetters maintaining the errata
extracted.subtask_description: Conventions and standards for recording, formatting, and publishing corrections, amendments, improvements, and plans to TAOCP Volume 4A; guidance for contributors who report errors or suggest changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change levels (\bugonpage, \amendpage, \improvepage, \planforpage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three (or four) levels of changes to the books are distinguished: "\bugonpage" introduces the correction of an error; "\amendpage" introduces new material for future editions; "\improvepage" introduces ameliorations of lesser importance. Also, "\planforpage" introduces some of the author's half-baked intentions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these four distinct typographic conventions to classify updates. The document explains that (depending on the \ifall flag) either three or four levels appear and shows examples of each. Keep the original keyword names and mark entries accordingly when recording a change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bug entries: mark and present critical errors
rubrics_metrics.description: "Technical or typographical errors (aka bugs) are the most critical items, so they are flagged with a `\thinspace{\manfnt x}\thinspace' preceding the page number."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For bugs: show the page and line, include the date on which the author was first told about the bug (this is the effective date on which the finder's fee is paid), and indicate necessary corrections straightforwardly (use the \becomes notation to show old -> new). Example: if the book says `n' where it should have said `n+1', show `n \becomes n+1'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments: new material for future editions
rubrics_metrics.description: "Amendments to the text appear in the same format as bugs, but without the `\thinspace{\manfnt x}\thinspace'. These are things I wish I had known about or thought of when I wrote the original text, so I added them later. The date is the date I drafted the new text."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record amendments with page/line and date, present replacement or added text clearly. Use same structural format as bug entries but do not prepend the bug-triangle marker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plans: author's tentative intentions
rubrics_metrics.description: "Plans for the future represent a third kind of item. In such notes I sketched my intentions about things that I wasn't ready to flesh out further when I wrote them down. You can identify these items because they're written in slanted type, and preceded by a bunch of dots ... leading to the date on which I recorded the plan in my files."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark plan entries with slanted type and dotted leaders to the date. Treat them as provisional notes of intent rather than definite corrections or insertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvements: minor ameliorations (often omitted from hardcopy)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The fourth and final category — indicated by page and line number in smaller, slanted type — consists of minor corrections or improvements that most readers don't want to know about, because they are so trivial. Changes introduced by \improvepage do not appear in the hardcopy listing."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify trivial wording/typographic tweaks as improvements. By default these may be omitted from the printed errata; include them only when the full (long form) errata is requested (controlled by an \ifall toggle). Use smaller/slanted typography to distinguish them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting conventions for change entries (page/line/date/context/replacement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Change entries show the macro (e.g., \bugonpage, \amendpage, \improvepage, \planforpage) followed by location like "4a.60 line 2" or "4a.xiv line 4", then the text showing the original and replacement, often using the \becomes notation. Dates are shown in yy.mm.dd format in parentheses after the entry header.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always include precise location (volume/page/line or exercise/answer identifiers), the date when the change was recorded (yy.mm.dd), and the exact textual replacement. Examples throughout the document demonstrate replacing single tokens, entire paragraphs, algorithm steps, equations, or bibliographic details. Keep consistent structure for machine- and human-readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of \becomes macro to show replacements
rubrics_metrics.description: The macro \becomes is defined so that when one thing should be replaced by another the change is shown thus: example: $n$ \becomes $n+1$.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display corrections with the \becomes arrow (a wiggly arrow glyph is used in print). Use this to make old->new transformations explicit and unambiguous. The document defines \becomes to print the arrow appropriately in math/text mode.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date display and century handling (\date and \hundred macros)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dates in entries are encoded as yy.mm.dd and converted by the \date macro to a display like "dd Mon 19yy". The \hundred macro controls the century printed (example sets \hundred{20} or 19).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When entering dates, use the yy.mm.dd encoding; the macros will expand to the desired textual date. Ensure the century macro (\hundred) is set appropriately for pre/post-1997 conventions when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finder's-fee/date semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: "The date on which I first was told about the bug is shown; this is the effective date on which I paid the finder's fee."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the date of notification (not necessarily date of author edit); use that date in the entry header. This documents when the reporter notified the author and is used for administrative/tracking purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructions for submitting comments to the author
rubrics_metrics.description: "Please let me know of any improvements that you think I ought to make. Send your comments either by snail mail to D. E. Knuth, Computer Science, Gates Building 1B, Stanford University, Stanford CA 94305-9015, or by email to taocp@cs.stanford.edu. (Use email for book suggestions only, please — all other correspondence is returned unread to the sender, or discarded, because I have no time to read ordinary email.) Although I'm working full time on Volume 4 these days, I will try to reply to all such messages within a year of receipt."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified submission channels: snail mail for general errata/edits, email only for book-suggestion-type comments. Expect up to one year for replies; other correspondence (not matching the requested type) may be returned unread.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of long-form/full errata online
rubrics_metrics.description: "My personal file of updates also includes a fourth category of items, not shown in this list. ... If you really want to see all of the gory details, you can download the full list from Internet webpage http://www-cs-faculty.stanford.edu/~knuth/taocp.html by selecting the 'long form' of the errata."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers/readers who want exhaustive/trivial updates should consult the online long-form errata. The printed/short errata omits many trivial improvements unless the \ifall flag is set to include them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typographic cues and emphasis rules for different change types
rubrics_metrics.description: The document prescribes typographic differences: bug entries get a black-triangle marker in the margin; plan entries are in slanted type and preceded by dots; improvement entries appear in smaller, slanted type; amendments look like bugs but lack the triangle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these typographic cues to visually communicate severity/intent of each entry. Maintain consistent font sizes and markers as shown in examples so readers can immediately distinguish categories.
